say: @Bram There you are! I’ve been running since Thornwick. Three days!
@Bram Dad sent me. Well. Dad said “don’t”. So I came.

choices.label: Go home, Bram.
say: @Bram No.
@Cael He’s not wrong to come. He’s wrong if he thinks it’ll be safe.
@Bram I don’t think that. I just think it’ll be worse without me.

choices.label: Good. Come with us.
say: @Bram I brought bread. Mira’s. Don’t tell her I took the good loaf.

choices.label: (Hug him.)
say: @Bram …Yeah. Me too.
@Bram They’re rebuilding. Mira says she doesn’t blame you. She says it every morning. Loudly. To everyone.
@Bram Two roofs are new thatch. Dad says the forge never looked better.
@Bram Not a roof lost. Wynn’s telling everyone the stone woke for you. They’re making a song of it. It’s bad.
@Cael South, then. There’s an Oruun cistern on this road. Old water, and a lesson in it.
steps.objective: Follow Cael south to the cistern

do.hint: Touch the water to draw a stream; drag to aim it. It reaches about eight metres from the pool.

say: @Bram Smoke! The camp, by the pool!
@Cael Someone left their fire. It’s in the tents now.
@Cael Water, then. It’s quieter than fire, and it goes where it’s let.
@Cael Touch the pool and draw it out. Aim at the flames, not the cloth that isn’t burning.
steps.objective: Put out the fires in the camp

say: @Cael That’s it. Now bring it round.
@Cael Stand between the pool and the fire. The water won’t reach further than it’s let.
@Cael Some of it’s gone. You saved the rest. That counts.
@Bram Whoever owns that tent is going to be furious. Not at us. Probably.
@Cael All of it, and nothing drowned that didn’t need to be. Good.
@Bram That was… that was amazing. You were amazing. Don’t let it go to your head.
@Cael The road runs on under the sluice. The Oruun opened it with water, not hands.
@Cael The wheel. Put a stream on it and hold it there.
steps.objective: Turn the wheel with a stream of water

say: @Bram Maybe get closer to the wheel? I’m just saying. I don’t know water.
@Bram It’s going up! The whole thing’s going up!
@Cael Water doesn’t push. It persuades. Remember that.
@Cael Saltmere’s past the throat. The sea, and a town that lives with it.
The sea! I’ve never seen the sea. Have you? You haven’t. Ha.
Cael doesn’t eat. Have you noticed? I’ve been watching.
Mira sent bread. I ate some. Most. The bread is a story now.
Dad says hello. He didn’t. But he would have.
You’re different. Not bad different. Taller, somehow.
Water remembers the shape of everything it touched. Be careful what you teach it.
Your friend talks a great deal.
I like him. Don’t tell him.
